name: Bill Hagerty
bio: Former U.S. Ambassador to Japan and Tennessee Commissioner of Economic and Community Development. Trump-endorsed; $5.3M cash on hand.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Hagerty has not published new positions on early childhood education, pre-K, or Head Start in 2025-2026. His most recent documented stance, from 2021, strongly opposed federal preschool expansion as 'cradle-to-grave, big-government dependency.'
early_childhood_ed.details: No press releases, floor statements, or campaign materials from Hagerty's Senate office or 2026 reelection campaign were found specifically addressing early childhood education, Head Start, or universal pre-K in 2025-2026. His 2021 opposition to the Build Back Better Act's nearly $400 billion universal pre-K proposal — which he called 'an unprecedented step toward displacing parents and indoctrinating American children' — remains the most recent on-record position. The One Big Beautiful Bill he supported in 2025 includes expanded employer childcare tax credits and 529 savings accounts but does not create new federal pre-K programs.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public statement from Hagerty on child hunger, SNAP, Summer EBT, or school nutrition programs was found in 2025-2026. He voted against the 2021 American Rescue Plan, which included SNAP expansions. Tennessee's SNAP junk food restriction and Summer EBT debates have been led by Gov. Bill Lee, with no documented Hagerty comment.
child_hunger.details: Hagerty voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan Act (March 2021), which included SNAP benefit increases and pandemic child nutrition provisions. The Tennessee SNAP junk food restriction waiver approved in late 2025 was a state-level initiative by Gov. Lee, and no Hagerty statement responding to it was found. Tennessee's refusal to participate in the federal Summer EBT/SUN Bucks program — rejecting $84 million in 2026 aid for roughly 700,000 children — was also a state executive decision with no documented Senate response from Hagerty. His general philosophy opposing expanded government welfare programs aligns with his 2021 voting record.

parental_support.summary: Hagerty actively supported and voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed into law in 2025, which expanded the Child Tax Credit to $2,200 per child, made permanent the employer paid family and medical leave tax credit, and quadrupled the employer childcare tax credit. He frames these as market-based tax relief rather than government-mandated programs.
parental_support.details: On June 30, 2025, Hagerty appeared on Bloomberg TV's Balance of Power to discuss Senate passage of the OBBB reconciliation package, calling it essential tax relief. The law he voted for expanded the Child Tax Credit to $2,200 per child (indexed for inflation), made permanent the employer-provided paid family and medical leave tax credit, quadrupled the maximum employer-provided childcare credit (up to $500,000; $600,000 for small businesses), and created Trump savings accounts seeded with $1,000 for infants born 2025-2028. Hagerty opposes government-mandated paid family leave, preferring employer tax incentives, and has not co-sponsored standalone paid leave legislation.

name: Marquita Bradshaw
bio: Memphis environmental justice activist who won the 2020 Democratic primary against expectations. Running again on environmental and economic-justice platform.
photo_credit: Bradshaw for Senate official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Bradshaw's 2026 campaign platform calls for funding education 'the same as we do our military,' and her 2020 platform explicitly included 'high quality public education pre-k-12' and providing 'quality childcare.' No new 2025-2026 early childhood-specific positions have been published.
early_childhood_ed.details: Bradshaw's current issues page states: 'I am a lifelong proponent of funding our education system the same as we do our military in order to promote generations of meaningful success regardless of background or location in Tennessee.' Her 2020 campaign platform explicitly called for 'high quality public education pre-k-12 that prepare students for success in higher education and workforce' and included 'provide quality childcare' among education priorities. No new 2025-2026 statements specifically addressing federal pre-K funding, Head Start, or childcare expansion programs were found in news searches or on her campaign site.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public position from Bradshaw on child hunger, SNAP, Summer EBT, or school nutrition programs was found in any 2025-2026 research. Her campaign site does not address food assistance.
child_hunger.details: Bradshaw's 2026 campaign issues page covers healthcare, criminal justice, gun safety, living wage, the Green New Deal, education, democracy, and DACA, but does not mention food assistance, SNAP, Summer EBT, or child nutrition programs. No news articles, interviews, or press releases from Bradshaw responding to Tennessee's refusal to participate in Summer EBT (rejecting $84 million in 2026 federal aid for roughly 700,000 children) or the state's SNAP junk food restriction waiver were found. OnTheIssues records no stance for Bradshaw on Welfare and Poverty.

parental_support.summary: Bradshaw advocates for a living wage of at least $15 per hour as a core economic support for working families, and her 2020 platform called for 'quality childcare.' No specific 2025-2026 positions on paid family leave, child tax credit, or childcare cost policy have been published.
parental_support.details: Bradshaw's current campaign platform calls for 'fully and aggressively fighting for the federal recognition and implementation of a living wage beginning at immediately increasing the minimum wage to $15.00 an hour.' Her 2020 platform included 'relieve current student debt, provide quality childcare' as part of her economic agenda. No 2025-2026 press releases, interviews, or campaign statements addressing the OBBB's child tax credit provisions, federal paid leave legislation, or childcare affordability were found. OnTheIssues records no stance from Bradshaw on the child tax credit, paid family leave, or childcare cost subsidy programs.

name: Maria Brewer
bio: Longtime Tennessee Democratic Party staffer making her first run for federal office.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position on early childhood education, pre-K, Head Start, or childcare programs has been found as of May 2026.
early_childhood_ed.details: Brewer's campaign, confirmed active as of her April 25, 2026 appearance on The Loyal Opposition podcast, has focused on broad themes of working-family economic concerns, healthcare, cost of living, and tax fairness. Her primary digital hub is a Linktree page (linktr.ee/mariabrewerforsenate); no standalone campaign website with a policy platform was located. She has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and no early childhood education positions were found in news searches, FEC filings, or her public campaign communications.

child_hunger.summary: No public position on SNAP, food assistance, Summer EBT, child nutrition programs, or school meals has been found as of May 2026.
child_hunger.details: Searches conducted May 2026 across Ballotpedia, her Linktree page, an April 25, 2026 podcast appearance on The Loyal Opposition, FEC filings, and general news sources returned no statements from Brewer on child hunger, SNAP, Summer EBT, or school meals. Her publicly discussed campaign priorities as of April 2026 include high cost of living, tax fairness, Citizens United, opposition to military intervention, and defense-contractor influence. Child nutrition programs were not mentioned in any source found.

parental_support.summary: No public position on paid family leave, child tax credit, childcare costs, or parental financial support has been found as of May 2026.
parental_support.details: Brewer has described her campaign as rooted in 'ordinary working-family experience' and 'healthcare and motherhood,' and her Linktree page describes her as an 'activist, organizer, daughter, mom, wife' running against 'the billionaire class that owns Washington.' No specific policy positions on paid family leave, child tax credit expansion, childcare cost relief, or related programs have been stated in any publicly accessible source. She has not completed the Ballotpedia 2026 Candidate Connection survey.
